title: Add support for global() function in CSS Modules animation names
author: jantimon
summary: Adds postcss-modules' `animation: global(name)` by having the unparsed-token serializer drop any `global(...)` function wrapper. The implementation can't land as is (it rewrites `global()` in every unparsed value, even without CSS modules, and works on raw tokens instead of the parsed animation-name), so the real question is whether to support this syntax at all.
evidence: devongovett on #825 (2024-10-07): "I think we probably will not support that syntax, but perhaps via a different one" (re :global keyframe names), pointing to css-modules/css-modules#390. On #863 (2024-12-18) he pointed to that proposal's "referencing an identifier" section as "a more general way"; when told postcss had shipped global(), he replied "Not sure. It was just a proposal. I was hoping to get consensus between implementations." No comments on the PR itself; 2 years old.
decision: Should CSS modules support postcss's `global(name)` for animation names (implemented in the parsed AnimationName under css_modules), or only the css-modules proposal's identifier-reference syntax, in which case this PR is closed?
